headline: The evidence can't tell yet. We'll know more when we have a full five years in the other states. Most of the range for 2–4 unit homes is above zero, but it includes a small fall, and there is enough noise that we're not sure it's caused by this reform.

timing.label: Measured slow start
timing.note: 2027 at the measured first-law-year share (about −21% of full size, from Oregon 2022, California 2022 and Vermont 2023), full size from 2028. Three single years: the sign of the 2027 share is not measured. With a negative share, the lower line's 2027 value sits slightly above zero.

side_measures.label: About +3,905 more homes over 5 years when we count all 1–4 unit buildings, including 1-unit homes on split lots and other single-unit types.
side_measures.caveat: Too noisy to include in predicted range because Census mixes these single units with conventional single-family homes.

side_measures.label: About +4,226 more homes over 5 years when we add our estimate for 5 and 6 unit buildings.
side_measures.caveat: Too noisy to include in predicted range because Census mixes 5 and 6 unit projects with all 5+ unit projects.

side_measures.label: About +7,888 more homes over 5 years. Counts every building size, so swings in house and apartment building swamp any change from this reform.
side_measures.caveat: Too noisy to include in predicted range.

extra_lines.label: With add-ons
extra_lines.info: The core plus estimated townhouses and split-lot homes (Census files them as 1-unit; records that include them show 1.5–3× the Census 2–4 count, middle 2.25×) and 5–6 unit buildings. Estimated, not measured.

extra_lines.label: Stronger reform (up to 6 homes per lot)
extra_lines.info: Possibility, not measured. Assumes that if 5–6 homes were allowed, new small buildings would split between 2–4 and 5–6 units the way past building did in OR, CA, ME and VT. None of the tested laws allowed 5–6 homes by right.

range90.unit: extra homes in 2–4 unit buildings permitted, 2027–2031
range90.method: The real four-state result (Oregon, California, Maine and Vermont against similar places in the same regions) placed against 10,000 sets of 4 fake law states drawn from 34 comparison states: the 5th to 95th percentile of their spread around the real result, in extra 2–4 unit homes per 1,000 single-family homes a year, times Wisconsin's 1,839,569 single-family homes.
range90.coverage: Built from fake-law estimates, so it already carries their spread and is not widened (shared rule 5). Most of the range is above zero, but it includes a small fall.
range90.years_method: Measured slow start: 2027 at about −21% of full size, full size from 2028.

range90_flat.unit: extra homes in 2–4 unit buildings permitted, 2027–2031
range90_flat.method: The real four-state result (Oregon, California, Maine and Vermont against similar places in the same regions) placed against 10,000 sets of 4 fake law states drawn from 34 comparison states: the 5th to 95th percentile of their spread around the real result, in extra 2–4 unit homes per 1,000 single-family homes a year, times Wisconsin's 1,839,569 single-family homes.
range90_flat.coverage: Built from fake-law estimates, so it already carries their spread and is not widened (shared rule 5). Most of the range is above zero, but it includes a small fall.

side_lines.label: Four-state measured result
side_lines.note: The real result in Oregon, California, Maine and Vermont against similar places, applied to Wisconsin.

side_lines.label: All 1–4 unit buildings
side_lines.note: Includes 1-unit homes on split lots and other single-unit types. Too noisy to include in predicted range because Census mixes these single units with conventional single-family homes.

side_lines.label: Adding 5 and 6 unit buildings
side_lines.note: Our estimate for 5 and 6 unit buildings added to all 1–4 unit buildings. Too noisy to include in predicted range because Census mixes 5 and 6 unit projects with all 5+ unit projects.

side_lines.label: All building sizes
side_lines.note: Its own range is -13,189 to 29,818. Counts every building size, so swings in house and apartment building swamp any change from this reform. Too noisy to include in predicted range.

side_lines.label: With townhouses, split-lot homes and 5–6 unit buildings
side_lines.note: Estimated, not measured: Census files townhouses as 1-unit.

side_lines.label: Stronger reform (up to 6 homes per lot)
side_lines.note: Possibility, not measured. Assumes new small buildings would split between 2–4 and 5–6 units the way past building did in OR, CA, ME and VT.
